extracted.intended_audience: researchers and organizations seeking DARPA funding (potential BAA proposers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for researchers and organizations preparing proposals in response to DARPA office-wide Broad Agency Announcements (BAAs), including what BAAs are, eligibility, scope alignment, where BAAs are posted, and how offices solicit out-of-priority ideas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of BAAs as primary vehicle for basic and applied R&D funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Our primary vehicle for funding basic and applied R&D programs is the Broad Agency Announcement (BAA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposers should plan to submit ideas and proposals through BAAs when seeking DARPA funding for basic or applied research efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Align proposal with the BAA's defined area of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: A program BAA defines an area of interest and specifies the type of award (contract, grant, or cooperative agreement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure your proposal addresses the specific technical area(s) outlined in the BAA and is suitable for the award type the BAA identifies (contract, grant, or cooperative agreement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: open to all proposers who meet agency needs
rubrics_metrics.description: BAAs are open to all proposers who can meet the agency’s needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While BAAs do not restrict proposers by organization type, proposals must demonstrably meet DARPA's stated technical needs and requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: No guarantee of award
rubrics_metrics.description: BAAs do not guarantee an award will be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposers should not assume selection; submission is an invitation to compete and does not imply funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Posting and publication requirement: System for Award Management
rubrics_metrics.description: All BAAs are posted to the federal government’s System for Award Management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposers should monitor SAM for current BAAs and official solicitation documents; use SAM as the authoritative posting for DARPA BAAs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office-wide BAAs allow out-of-priority idea submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Each of our technical offices maintains a dedicated BAA to enable researchers to propose ideas that may fall outside our current priorities but have potential value to national security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have a novel idea not explicitly listed in current priorities, consider submitting it under the office-wide BAA if you can justify its potential national security value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office BAAs outline current technical areas of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: To guide proposers, each office-wide BAA outlines the office’s current technical areas of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read the office-wide BAA to understand the office's prioritized technical topics and tailor proposals to those areas when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office-wide BAAs are refreshed annually
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for updated BAAs regularly (at least annually) to ensure proposals respond to the most current stated interests and priorities.
